releases.body:
# Amber 2.0.0-beta.14

Amber 2.0.0-beta.14 lets an app drop libz and OpenSSL, runs its cryptography
on Beryl at hardware speed, runs every regex on Mica, and applies
`logging.severity` from the environment file.

## An app can link no libz and no OpenSSL

Built with `-Dwithout_zlib -Dwithout_openssl`, an `amber new -d sqlite` app
with a scaffold, on Amber CLI 2.0.15, links none of PCRE2, libyaml, GMP,
libz, libssl or libcrypto (`otool -L` and `nm -u` both show none). It still
gzips its responses, accepts a form `POST`, and refuses a gzip request body
and a `charset=UTF-7` form with `415`. Under load at the 8 MiB starting heap
it peaked at 17.4 to 17.5 MiB of RSS on an M4 Mac mini, against 19.8 to
19.9 MiB for the default build of the same app.

The flags are opt-in. A default build still links libz and OpenSSL, because
Crystal's own `HTTP` and `OpenSSL` code requires them.

- `-Dwithout_zlib`: `Amber::Pipe::Compression` gzips and deflates with a
  pinned copy of Mica's DEFLATE, in Crystal, in every build. Grant's
  compressed columns and asset_pipeline's precompressed assets and stored
  pages use Mica too. `idle_compressors:` and the compressor pool are gone;
  a gzip response carries no modification time.
- `-Dwithout_openssl`: cookie signing and encryption, flash, encrypted files
  and COSE run on a pinned copy of Beryl. OpenSSL remains only for TLS, so
  the flag suits an app whose TLS ends at a proxy; in such a build
  `server.ssl` and mailer `use_tls` raise
  `Amber::Exceptions::TLSNotCompiledIn`.

## Cryptography on Beryl, at hardware speed

Encrypted cookies, encrypted sessions and `FileEncryptor` now write message
format version 2 (XChaCha20-Poly1305 under an HKDF-SHA256 key). Version 1
values are still read under the current and every previous secret and are
rewritten in version 2 on their next save. An app that rolls back to an
earlier beta after writing version 2 values signs its visitors out once.
`MessageVerifier` and `MessageEncryptor` accept `:sha256`, `:sha384`,
`:sha512` and `:sha1`; any other digest raises `ArgumentError` at
construction.

Beryl is pinned at amberframework/beryl `7d678c08`. Its hashes, HMAC and
AEADs run on the processor's SHA, AES, carry-less multiply and vector
instructions on Apple Silicon, Linux AArch64 and x86-64, and Beryl measures
every one at least as fast as OpenSSL 4.1.0 on an Apple M1 Max.

## Every regex runs on Mica

Every regex in Amber compiles on Mica, the default `Regex` engine of
crystal-alpha from 1.21.0-incremental-6, and CI checks each one.
`HTML.encode_entities` and `Amber::Markdown::HTMLEntities::Encoder` are
removed: no program that called them ever compiled.

## `logging.severity` sets the log level (#1461)

`logging.severity` (and `AMBER_LOGGING_SEVERITY`) was read but never
applied, so every app logged at `info`. An app now applies it once at boot:

```crystal
Amber.settings.logging.apply_severity_to_log
Amber::Server.start
```

Amber CLI 2.0.15 writes that line into `src/<app>.cr`. An app generated
earlier adds it after its last `require`.

## Performance guide

`docs/guides/performance.md` (#1471) gives the patterns, tools and settings
that make an Amber app fast and small from its first build, each with the
measurement it rests on.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.15 for new apps; it pins Amber `v2.0.0-beta.14`, Grant
`v0.26.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.39.0`. For an existing app, pin the three
release commits in `shard.yml`, run `minecart update amber grant
asset_pipeline`, add the `apply_severity_to_log` line, and run
`amber setup:agent`. Grant 0.26.0 writes encrypted attributes in format
version 2, which Grant 0.25.1 cannot read, so roll back only before new
values are written.

An app compiled with asset_pipeline 0.39.0 can be built with `-Dwithout_zlib -Dwithout_openssl` and link neither libz nor OpenSSL. An ordinary build behaves as 0.38.0 did.

- **No libz with `-Dwithout_zlib`.** Precompressed assets (`app.css.gz`) and the page cache's stored pages are gzipped by a pinned copy of Mica's DEFLATE, in Crystal (`AssetPipeline::GzipCoding`). Both encoders write one gzip member at level 6 with no modification time; their bytes differ, so a `.gz` file and a stored page's gzip `ETag` change when an app turns the flag on.
- **No OpenSSL with `-Dwithout_openssl`.** Fingerprints, Subresource Integrity values and page-cache keys are hashed by a pinned copy of Beryl's SHA-256 (`AssetPipeline::SHA256Digest`). The digests are the same bytes, so fingerprints and cache keys do not change. On Apple Silicon, Linux AArch64 and x86-64 Beryl hashes with the processor's SHA instructions.
- Mica is pinned at amberframework/mica `37e8b019` (faster Inflate) and Beryl at amberframework/beryl `7d678c08` (hardware hashes and AEADs), each by commit and per-file sha256. The flags need Crystal 1.21 or newer.
- `scripts/check_default_require_linkage.rb` builds its probes with both flags and checks for no libz, libssl or libcrypto; CI checks every regex against Mica.

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.21.0-incremental-8

Tracks upstream [Crystal 1.21.0](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.21.0) and includes everything in 1.21.0-incremental-7.

### Fixed

- **Non-release programs link on Linux again** ([#26](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/26)). 1.21.0-incremental-7 named the function of a proc literal `~proc<type>@<enclosing function>`. An ELF linker reads `name@text` as version *text* of *name*, and GNU ld defines an absolute symbol named *text*: the enclosing function itself. Every non-release program whose proc function was referred to from another object file failed to link with `multiple definition of` errors such as `*GC::add_finalizer_impl<File>:Nil` and `~Crystal::System::Signal::segfault_handler:init` (Homebrew Formula CI run 45076394682, crimson-knight/homebrew-agent-crystal#17). The proc function is now `~proc<type>~in~<enclosing function>`; macOS was not affected.

### Faster incremental builds

- **IR skip** ([#25](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/25)): in an `--incremental` build, a module whose inputs did not change gets no LLVM IR, and its cached object file carries over. Grant300 body edit: 78 s wall (was 167 s), IR generation 8.7 s (was about 45 s). `CRYSTAL_IR_SKIP=0` turns it off; `CRYSTAL_IR_SKIP_VERIFY=1` generates every module and fails the build when a skipped module would have given other bitcode.

### Checked

- Linux arm64 container (Ubuntu 26.04, GNU ld 2.46, image `crystallang/crystal:1.22.1@sha256:1ed8297a705eae76d88bc146ce83d0b00dc014bb201df6d93c024e20c14dbfce`): the compiler at 9cbbe3180 fails `seed_macro_run.cr` with 29 multiple definitions; this tag's tree links it, seeds `ecr/process.cr`, and passes `stable_numbering_spec.cr` and `ir_skip_spec.cr` (27 examples, 0 failures).
- macOS arm64: `spec/compiler/codegen` 1889 examples, 0 failures (2 known `special_vars_spec.cr:18` errors); `spec/compiler/semantic` 3427 examples, 0 failures; `spec/compiler-cli` 42 examples, 0 failures; incremental rebuild, release units and IR skip specs 25 examples, 0 failures; stage-2 self-host (non-release, `--threads 8`) with its codegen block/closure/proc specs 219 examples, 0 failures, and std array/hash/string/set specs 1678 examples (3 known `String#encode` failures).

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.21.0-incremental-8`, commit `d382251e6b5aa10dba6652d27d91efb370f2c5f5`.
- GitHub source archive `https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/archive/refs/tags/v1.21.0-incremental-8.tar.gz` (the URL the Homebrew formula pins): sha256 `832ffc5b3bb517f5e66e612d9719519026fedfe93b9263155b9b5f0c12086946` (downloaded twice, same hash; `git get-tar-commit-id` gives the commit above).

Install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install crimson-knight/agent-crystal/agent-crystal
```

Or build from source:
```bash
git clone --branch v1.21.0-incremental-8 https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal
cd crystal
LLVM_CONFIG=$(brew --prefix llvm@21)/bin/llvm-config make crystal macro_run_seed release=1
```

## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.21.0-incremental-7

Tracks upstream [Crystal 1.21.0](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.21.0) and includes everything in 1.21.0-incremental-6, where `Regex` and `YAML` run on [Mica](https://github.com/amberframework/mica)'s engines by default.

> **Known issue, Linux:** on ubuntu-24.04 the compiler builds, but linking a program fails with `multiple definition of` errors between its per-type objects (Homebrew Formula CI run 45076394682, crimson-knight/homebrew-agent-crystal#17). The Homebrew formula stays off this tag until that is fixed. macOS arm64 builds and runs programs.

### Memory

- **`HTTP::Server::RequestProcessor` keeps `skip_to_end`'s 32 KiB stack buffer out of `#process`** ([#23](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/23)). Inlined, it grew `#process`'s frame from 0x190 to 0x8130 bytes, so every connection fiber ran its handlers 32 KiB deeper.
- **Release units are contiguous runs of functions** ([#24](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/24)). `--release` splits the module into parts that keep the single-object build's function order, so code that runs together stays on the same pages of the executable.
- `spec/compiler`: a regression spec pins the compile error for Grant's old `RAW_JOIN_TARGET` lookahead on Mica, which names `-Duse_pcre2` ([#22](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/22)).

### Measured

macOS arm64, this compiler built from the tag's source archive; an `amber new -d sqlite` app (Amber CLI 2.0.14, Amber v2.0.0-beta.13, Grant v0.25.1) with a scaffolded Post, `--release`, Homebrew's 4 KB libgc, 8 MiB starting heap, one form POST, then 15 s of `GET /` and 15 s of `GET /posts/new` at 32 connections. Peak RSS in MiB, interleaved rounds on the same machine:

| Compiler | Peak RSS | Binary bytes |
|---|---|---:|
| 1.21.0-incremental-4 | 19.89 / 19.91 (one 18.66) | 3,987,696 |
| 1.21.0-incremental-6 | 20.86 / 20.92 / 20.84 | 4,150,256 |
| **1.21.0-incremental-7** | **20.48 / 20.55 / 20.52 / 20.66 / 20.59 / 20.63** | 4,149,968 |
| 1.21.0-incremental-7, `-Duse_pcre2` | 20.70 / 20.55 | 4,097,296 |
| 1.21.0-incremental-7, `-Duse_pcre2 -Duse_libyaml` | 20.75 / 20.69 | 3,987,888 |

This release takes back about 0.35 MiB of incremental-6's peak; about 0.7 MiB above incremental-4 remains and does not come from the Mica engines (selecting PCRE2 and libyaml leaves it in place).

The same compiler builds an app with associations, association, aliased raw, nested and left outer joins and an array-union `where`; it runs on `Regex::MicaEngine`, links no PCRE2, and serves its scaffold pages and a CSRF form POST.

### Provenance

- Tag `v1.21.0-incremental-7`, commit `fdb5c566818d157c1d951962a0ba003742adfc63`.
- GitHub source archive `https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/archive/refs/tags/v1.21.0-incremental-7.tar.gz` (the URL the Homebrew formula pins): sha256 `b7c00a91cfbf058c7de28012abbc18af7b69ecd9b2bca3bd120ded39e2bdb0ec` (downloaded twice, same hash).

Install via Homebrew:
```bash
brew install crimson-knight/agent-crystal/agent-crystal
```

Or build from source:
```bash
git clone --branch v1.21.0-incremental-7 https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal
cd crystal
LLVM_CONFIG=$(brew --prefix llvm@21)/bin/llvm-config make crystal macro_run_seed release=1
```

Grant 0.25.1 runs every regex it holds on Mica, the default `Regex` engine of crystal-alpha from 1.21.0-incremental-6. Upgrade from 0.25.0 needs no code change.

- **Fix: `where` with a union of arrays compiles on a Mica-default compiler.** `where(id: list)` with, for example, `Array(Int64) | Array(Range(Int64, Int64))` ran a lookbehind, possessive and lookahead pattern inside a macro, and the compiler runs macro regexes on its own engine, so the build stopped and `-Duse_pcre2` did not help. The rooting is now three substitutions without lookaround (`Grant::Query::TypeNameRooting`); on PCRE2 they give the same text the old pattern gave.
- **Fix: a table rebuild no longer raises on Mica.** `Grant::Schema::TableRebuild::Scanner.mentions?` built a lookaround pattern at run time; it now consumes the neighboring characters instead.
- The lookahead in `RAW_JOIN_TARGET` left Grant in 0.24.0. An app on Grant 0.23.4 or older that uses joins does not compile on a Mica-default compiler; upgrade to this release.
- Specs compare each rewrite with the pattern it replaced on PCRE2 and check fixed examples on every engine.
- CI checks every regex in `src`, `spec`, `scripts`, `bench` and `examples` against Mica's dialect (`scripts/check_regex_literals.cr` from amberframework/mica, pinned by commit and Git tree).

No API changes. Minimum Crystal: 1.19.0. Merged in #79.

releases.body:
## Crystal Alpha with Incremental Compilation — 1.21.0-incremental-6

Tracks upstream [Crystal 1.21.0](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/releases/tag/1.21.0) and includes everything in 1.21.0-incremental-5. In this release `Regex` and `YAML` run on [Mica](https://github.com/amberframework/mica)'s engines by default, so a program links neither PCRE2 nor libyaml ([#19](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/19), on top of [#17](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/17) and [#18](https://github.com/crimson-knight/crystal/pull/18)).

### Mica is the default Regex and YAML engine

| Build | Regex | YAML |
|---|---|---|
| `crystal build app.cr` | Mica | Mica |
| `-Duse_pcre2` | PCRE2 | Mica |
| `-Duse_libyaml` | Mica | libyaml |
| `-Duse_pcre2 -Duse_libyaml` | PCRE2 | libyaml (what 1.21.0-incremental-5 builds by default) |
| `-Duse_pcre`, or `USE_PCRE1` set | legacy PCRE | Mica |
| `-Duse_mica` | Mica | Mica (the flag is still accepted) |

- **Regex.** Searches run in time linear in the haystack and no C regex library is linked. On a production Amber V2 app (the Scribe license server) CPU, memory and latency per request were equal to PCRE2 within the 95% intervals on every route, with 370 of 370 app specs on both engines and a release binary 1.21 times as large.
- **YAML.** Mica reads and writes as libyaml 0.2.5 does: yaml-test-suite 402 of 402, 6,000,000 generated documents compared against libyaml with 0 disagreements, parsing 1.5 to 1.9 times as fast, the emitter 14% slower on a 2.1 MB document.
- **What may need a change in your program.** A regex literal that uses lookaround, a backreference, an atomic group, recursion, a conditional, `\K` or a verb, in code the program reaches, is now a compile error that names the way out: rewrite it (`doc/regex_mica.md` lists rewrites) or build with `-Duse_pcre2`. A pattern built at run time raises `Regex::UnsupportedSyntaxError`. For libyaml's own readings where they differ (`doc/yaml_mica.md`, "Differences"), build with `-Duse_libyaml`.
- A program built with an opt-out needs that C library where it is built and where it runs, as before.

### Compiler fix

- `ReferenceStorage(T)` accepts a class that has subclasses. It used to refuse the class's virtual type, which stopped a program with a generic subclass of `Array` or `Hash` (`class First(T) < Array(T)`) from compiling on the Mica engines.

### Verification

Run on the merged tree (macOS arm64, LLVM 21.1.8; local suites, this fork's GitHub Actions are disabled):

- Regex specs: 155 examples, 0 failures on Mica; 147, 0 failures with `-Duse_pcre2` and with `-Duse_pcre`.
- Regex + string specs: 2799 examples on Mica and 2793 with `-Duse_pcre2`, each with the 3 `String#encode` examples that also fail on 1.21.0-incremental-5 on this machine.
- YAML specs: 465 examples, 0 failures on Mica and with `-Duse_libyaml`.
- Full compiler suite: 13857 examples, 0 failures, 2 errors (`special_vars_spec.cr:18`, the same 2 as on 1.21.0-incremental-5, and the same with the legacy PCRE engine selected).
- Markd 681 examples, Amber CLI 779, Minecart 387 unit and 423 integration: 0 failures.

Grant 0.25.0 makes BigDecimal support opt-in, so an app without decimal columns no longer links libgmp.

**An app with `BigDecimal` columns must add one line.** Put `require "grant/big_decimal"` above `require "grant"`:

```crystal
require "grant/big_decimal"
require "grant"
```

Without that line, a `BigDecimal` column, `sum(as: BigDecimal)` or a late `require "grant/big_decimal"` stops at compile time with a message that names the require. An app that already requires `big` before `grant` has the support without the file. Apps without decimal columns need no change.

- **GMP-free default path.** Grant's default path requires `big` nowhere. `scripts/check_gmp_linkage.rb` builds probe apps and fails if their binaries link GMP; CI runs it.
- **With the opt-in**, `BigDecimal` columns (`precision:`, `scale:`), `BigDecimal` and `Array(BigDecimal)` in `Grant::Columns::Type`, BigDecimal column defaults, exact decimal sums and `sum(as: BigDecimal)` behave as in 0.24.0. `Grant::BIG_DECIMAL_SUPPORT` is true when it is compiled in.
- **Without it, the sum of an expression or joined column** is an `Int64` when it is a whole number in range and a `Float64` otherwise (it was an `Int64` or a `BigDecimal`). Sums of integer and float columns are unchanged.
- **Fix: a `BigDecimal` column on MySQL reads every digit.** crystal-mysql decodes a DECIMAL as a `Float64`, so values past about 17 significant digits came back rounded. Grant now reads a DECIMAL as the exact text MySQL sends.
- `src/grant/converters/decimal.cr` is now `src/grant/converters/small_integer.cr` (`Grant::Converters::SmallInteger`) and `src/grant/big_decimal/decimal_converter.cr` (`Grant::Converters::Decimal`).

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.13

Amber 2.0.0-beta.13 is a security release. It holds the `charset` a client
names on a form to the WHATWG Encoding Standard.

## Security: a form's `charset` is held to the WHATWG Encoding Standard (#1460)

Through beta.12 the `charset` a client declared on a URL-encoded form went
straight to iconv, so on Linux a request could open any converter glibc ships
by naming it. From beta.13 Amber accepts only the labels of the
[WHATWG Encoding Standard](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#names-and-labels),
in any letter case, and each label opens the one decoder Amber maps it to.

A form whose `charset` is anything else is answered
`415 Unsupported Media Type` before its body is read. That covers `UTF-7`,
`ISO-2022-CN-EXT`, an empty or oversized name, and the standard's
`replacement`, `x-user-defined`, `windows-1255` and `windows-1258` encodings
(glibc decodes the last two by holding back the final letter). The request
raises `Amber::Exceptions::UnsupportedCharset`, a `BadRequest`, and a schema
parse reports it as `unsupported_media_type`. A UTF-8 label parses the form
directly, with no converter. Multipart and JSON bodies never took an encoding
name from the request and behave as before.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Every app on beta.12 or earlier should upgrade. Use Amber CLI 2.0.13 for new
apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit in `shard.yml`, run
`minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`. Amber CLI 2.0.13 also
moves new apps to Grant `v0.25.0`, whose `BigDecimal` support is opt-in: an
app with `BigDecimal` columns adds `require "grant/big_decimal"` above
`require "grant"`. asset_pipeline stays at `v0.38.0`.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.12

Amber 2.0.0-beta.12 makes a default app smaller in memory and safer at the
door: it refuses compressed request bodies, stops keeping a session for every
visitor, and allocates less on every request.

## What changed

- **Compressed request bodies are refused (#1454).** A request with a
  compressed body is answered `415 Unsupported Media Type` before routing or
  any pipe reads it. Crystal before 1.21.1 inflates gzip and deflate request
  bodies with no size limit
  ([GHSA-jfq5-c3x6-w7jj](https://github.com/crystal-lang/crystal/security/advisories/GHSA-jfq5-c3x6-w7jj)),
  so a 1 MiB body could become 1 GiB. The guard works on every compiler,
  crystal-alpha 1.21.0 included. An app that accepts compressed uploads sets
  `params.accepts_encoded_request_bodies: true` and bounds the body itself.
- **Sessions follow `session.store` (#1455).** See the behavior change below.
  `Amber::Pipe::Flash` writes the session only when there is a flash to keep
  or clear, so a visitor who never sees a flash gets no session. The memory
  session adapter keeps at most `session.max_memory_sessions` sessions
  (10,000 by default) and drops the one used longest ago. A `:web` route
  served to cookieless clients used to grow to 858 MiB in 90 s; it now stays
  under 15 MiB.
- **The logger allocates nothing when its lines are filtered (#1456).** At the
  default `info` level `Amber::Pipe::Logger` used to build every debug line,
  parse the params and create a session, about 11.8 KB per request, before
  `Log` dropped it.
- **`Amber::Pipe::Compression` (#1457).** It gzips or deflates responses with
  the same bytes as `HTTP::CompressHandler`, but its zlib streams come from
  `malloc` and are reused through a small pool, where `HTTP::CompressHandler`
  allocates about 270 KB from the collected heap for every compressed
  response. Amber CLI 2.0.12 apps use it through `CompressedResponsePipe`.
- **Asset tags are rendered once per manifest (#1458).** `stylesheet_link_tag`,
  `javascript_include_tag`, `image_tag`, `favicon_tag` and
  `javascript_importmap_tag` return stored HTML on later calls. A generated
  layout's three tags used to cost 6.9 KB per page.

## Behavior change: `signed_cookie` sessions live in the cookie

`store: signed_cookie` is the default in every generated app. Through beta.11
every store, `signed_cookie` included, kept sessions in the server's memory.
From beta.12 a `signed_cookie` or `encrypted_cookie` app keeps the session in
the visitor's cookie and nothing on the server. Session values travel with
every request and must fit in a 4,096-byte cookie (a larger session raises
`Amber::Exceptions::CookieOverflow`), the visitor can read (but not change) a
`signed_cookie` session, and `regenerate_session!` does nothing. An app that
needs server-side sessions sets `store: adapter` under `session:`, or
`AMBER_SESSION_STORE=adapter`.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.12 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit
in `shard.yml`, keep Grant `v0.24.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.38.0`, run
`minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`. Check the `session:`
section of each `config/environments/*.yml` against the behavior change above.
To use the pooled compressor, make the generated `CompressedResponsePipe` a
subclass of `Amber::Pipe::Compression` with an empty body, or plug
`Amber::Pipe::Compression.new` in its place. New apps start the collector's
heap at 8 MiB (`gc_initial_heap_mib: 8` under `server:`).

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.11

Amber 2.0.0-beta.11 carries the regex-free path from a JSON API to the whole
default app. An app made with `amber new -d sqlite`, with a Grant model and
asset_pipeline, links no PCRE2.

## What changed

- **No PCRE2 in a default app.** Grant 0.24.0 and asset_pipeline 0.38.0 keep
  `Regex` off their default require paths. The app Amber CLI 2.0.11 generates
  shows no `libpcre2` in `otool -L` or `ldd` and no `pcre2_` symbol in `nm`,
  before and after `amber generate scaffold` adds a Grant model. Amber CLI CI
  runs this check on macOS and Linux, and its control program that uses `Regex`
  must show PCRE2.
- **`respond_with` takes a `NamedTuple` (#1425, #1451).** The documented call now
  compiles. The tuple becomes `Hash(String, JSON::Any)` through its JSON form, so
  `Int32`, arrays and nested tuples work as values. `scripts/check_linkage.sh`
  answers one route this way.
- **`respond_with` takes any JSON-serializable `Hash` (#1451).**
  `Hash(String, String)`, `Hash(Symbol, Int32)` and the like used to fail to
  compile.
- **`Accept` q values count (#1451).** `respond_with` picks among the formats the
  response schema declares and honors `q`. `application/cbor;q=0` no longer
  answers CBOR, and a JSON-only schema answers JSON when JSON is acceptable.
- **A starting heap for the garbage collector (#1452).**
  `server.gc_initial_heap_mib` grows the collector's heap to that many MiB in
  every server process before it takes requests, and
  `AMBER_SERVER_GC_INITIAL_HEAP_MIB` overrides it. The default, 0, keeps the
  collector's own starting size, so existing apps see no change. Amber CLI 2.0.11
  writes 16 into every generated environment file.

## Keeping your app free of PCRE2

An app links PCRE2 again when it uses any of these, and it keeps working:

- `pattern:`, `filename_pattern:` or a custom `format:` on a schema field, and
  `validates_pattern` or a custom `validates_format`
- a `Regex` passed to `Pipe::CORS`, `Validator::Pattern` or `Validator::Format`
- Markdown, `strip_tags`, and the other `String` checks such as `email?` and `phone?`
- `request.cookies`; read `cookies` instead
- `require "grant/regex"` (for `validates_format_of`, the SQLite `REGEXP`
  operator and Regex entries in `filter_attributes`), and Grant's schema
  tooling, schema tenancy and sharding
- `Regex` in your own code

## Breaking changes

None in Amber. Grant 0.24.0 moves `validates_format_of` behind
`require "grant/regex"`; its release notes list the rest.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.11 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit
in `shard.yml`, along with Grant `v0.24.0` and asset_pipeline `v0.38.0`, run
`minecart update amber grant asset_pipeline`, and run `amber setup:agent`. To
start the collector's heap at the size new apps use, set
`gc_initial_heap_mib: 16` under `server:` in each `config/environments/*.yml`.

- **Regex-free default path.** Models, attributes, associations, querying, ordering, joins, saving, validation, i18n, logging, the query cache, transactions, the migrator and both the SQLite and PostgreSQL adapters use hand-written checks (`Grant::TextMatching`, `Grant::CharacterClass`). Each is compared with the pattern it replaced over edge cases, a seeded fuzz corpus and every Unicode code point.
- **Opt-in `require "grant/regex"`** turns on `validates_format_of`, Regex entries in `filter_attributes`, the SQLite `REGEXP` operator, and `EMAIL_REGEX`/`URL_REGEX`. Without it, those macros stop at compile time with a message that names the require. `validates_email` and `validates_url` need no opt-in.
- **Word characters follow PCRE2 10.43 and later on every platform**, including Linux runners that ship 10.42.
- **#43:** raw `Model.all` clauses containing ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET, GROUP BY or HAVING run as written.
- **#72 follow-up:** polymorphic and STI registries, `sti_root`, `AssociationLoader` and array `where` conditions root model types with `::`.
- `Model.migrator` compiles in an app that requires only the SQLite adapter.

Schema tooling, schema tenancy, sharding and `spec_support` still use Regex and link PCRE2 only when an app uses them.

Merged in #73.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.10

Amber 2.0.0-beta.10 takes the regex engine out of the request path. A JSON API
built on it links no PCRE2 on stock Crystal, and CI now fails if that changes.

## What changed

- **No PCRE2 in a JSON API.** On stock Crystal 1.22.2, an app with one GET and
  one POST shows no `libpcre2` in `otool -L` or `ldd` and no `pcre2_` symbol in
  `nm`, on macOS and on Linux. `scripts/check_linkage.sh` runs in CI, and its
  control program that uses `Regex` must show PCRE2.
- **Typed route rules (#1442).** Route parameter rules are types, and the router
  uses no regex engine.
- **Fixed patterns became plain code (#1443, #1444).** Amber's internal fixed
  patterns read strings directly, and no pattern uses lookaround.
- **Cookies, form keys, formats and backtraces (#1445).** The `Cookie` header,
  form keys, named schema formats, `String#url?`, backtrace frames and the
  exception page's code coloring use hand-written checks. Each check was compared
  with the pattern it replaced on generated input.
- **A crash removed.** `Validator::Format` with `FormatType::URL` raised
  `Regex::Error` on short crafted input. The new check takes time in proportion
  to the input.
- **One bad cookie no longer fails a request.** Amber leaves that pair out and
  keeps the others.

## Keeping your app free of PCRE2

An app links PCRE2 again when it uses any of these, and it keeps working:

- `pattern:`, `filename_pattern:` or a custom `format:` on a schema field, and
  `validates_pattern` or a custom `validates_format`
- a `Regex` passed to `Pipe::CORS`, `Validator::Pattern` or `Validator::Format`
- Markdown, `strip_tags`, and the other `String` checks such as `email?` and `phone?`
- `request.cookies`; read `cookies` instead
- Grant, whose query code uses `Regex` today
- `Regex` in your own code

## Breaking changes

- A route constraint is a rule, and a `Regex` no longer compiles. Replace
  `{"id" => /\d+/}` with `{"id" => :numeric}`. A rule judges the whole segment,
  so `{"cart" => /\d\d\d/}`, which matched `he110`, becomes
  `NUMERIC.with_length(3)`.
- A `Set-Cookie` header on a request is ignored. Specs that replayed response
  headers as a request must send `Cookie`.
- `Validator::Format::PATTERNS` is removed.
- Backtracer `app_dirs_pattern` is now the prefix list `list_of_app_directories`,
  and `modules_path_pattern` is now the prefix `modules_directory`.
- `Pipe::CORS` copies its origin list when it is built, and `cors.origins` holds
  strings and rule procs. `CORS.new` still accepts `CORS::OriginType`, and now
  also `Array(String)`.
- Phone numbers and the host of a `FormatType::URL` value accept ASCII digits only.
- The schema examples moved to `examples/schema`.

`CHANGELOG.md` has the complete list.

## Upgrading

Use Amber CLI 2.0.10 for new apps. For an existing app, pin the release commit in
`shard.yml`, run `minecart update amber`, and run `amber setup:agent`.

## Pin this release

Tarball sha256: 94a8315546063132454f995ea92472bd93ebb5192b1efa8838ed96f3f7aece1c

## Minecart 2025.11.25.9

Hardens `install --frozen` against a hostile dependency:

- Reused copies are checked against their locked source, and any `lib/` entry the lock does not list fails by name.
- A postinstall script that changes another installed copy, adds a `lib/` entry or changes `shard.lock` stops the install by name. The checks and cleanup also run when the script fails.

- New lock entries record `sha256-v2:` checksums. Existing `git-tree:` and `sha256:` entries keep verifying.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.9

Amber 2.0.0-beta.9 adds what an application needs behind a proxy, adds a
security headers pipe, and ships its rules and guides with the framework, so a
language server and a coding assistant know them from the first edit.

## What changed

- **Trusted proxies (#1415).** `server.trusted_proxies` lists the proxies
  allowed to report a client's address and scheme. Amber resolves the client IP
  and decides HTTPS from those proxies only, reads one forwarding header family,
  and validates the setting before it starts serving.
- **UNIX socket listener (#1415).** An application can listen on a UNIX socket.
  The socket is created owner-and-group only, and a bind lock stops two
  processes from taking the same path.
- **`Amber::Pipe::SecurityHeaders` (#1422).** Sends `X-Content-Type-Options`,
  `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy` and `Referrer-Policy`, set through
  a typed `security_headers` section. Plug it into each browser, API and static
  pipeline. See the migration guide.
- **Rule pack for amber-lsp.** `.amber-lsp/packs/amber_v2.yml` checks for Grant
  models, the V2 security headers pipe, ECR views, the JSON perimeter, nil
  narrowing and output through `Log`. Each finding names the fix. Amber CLI 2.0.9
  or newer loads the pack with no setup and prints its guidance at the start of
  an assistant session.
- **API card for amber-lsp.** `amber-lsp lookup` now carries verified notes and
  compiler-error hints for Amber's controller, params, testing and job APIs.
  Public params and validator methods declare concrete return types.
- **Guides for coding assistants.** `minecart install` now copies every guide
  in `docs/guides/` into the application's `.claude/skills/`, with an index skill.

## Upgrade

New applications from Amber CLI 2.0.9 start on this release. For an existing one:

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.9
```

Then run `minecart update amber`. If the application runs behind a proxy, list
the proxy in `server.trusted_proxies`, because Amber reads forwarding headers from
listed proxies only. `HTTPS: on` is not read as a scheme signal.

An application that calls `Amber::Validators::Params` directly now sees declared
return types. Code that relied on the earlier inferred unions may need a change
at compile time.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.9`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.9` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.8

Amber 2.0.0-beta.8 compiles on every Crystal version its `shard.yml`
declares, starting at 1.20.0, and lets an application choose the cache
policy for the static files it serves.

## What changed

- **Builds on Crystal 1.20 (#1434).** Beta.7 did not compile on Crystal
  1.20.x (`no parameter named 'writable'`), although it declares
  `crystal: ">= 1.20.0"`. Both `IO::Memory` calls now pass the read-only
  flag positionally, and CI runs the full suite on Crystal 1.20.0 next to
  1.22.1 and crystal-alpha.
- **Static files follow the application's cache policy (#1435).**
  `Amber::Pipe::Static` keeps a `Cache-Control` that an earlier handler
  already set. An application with its own fingerprint scheme overrides
  `#cache_control` in a subclass; the hook runs only for a file the pipe
  serves:

  ```crystal
  class AppStatic < Amber::Pipe::Static
    SHORT_FINGERPRINT = /-[0-9a-f]{8}\.[^\/]+$/i

    protected def cache_control(request_path : String) : String
      return IMMUTABLE_CACHE_CONTROL if request_path.matches?(SHORT_FINGERPRINT)
      super
    end
  end
  ```

  Asset headers now go on GET and HEAD responses only.

## Upgrade

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.8
```

Then run `minecart update amber`. An application that re-applied its own
`Cache-Control` after `super` in an `apply_asset_headers` override can move
that policy into `#cache_control`.

Amber CLI 2.0.8 generates projects on `2.0.0-beta.7`; change `version:` to
`2.0.0-beta.8` after `amber new`.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.8`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.8` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

# Amber 2.0.0-beta.7

Amber 2.0.0-beta.7 makes the fixes that AgentC applications carried on a
fork part of Amber itself, so those applications can depend on an official
release again. It also routes `.md` paths to the routes that declare them,
bounds request parameter parsing, and reads credentials from a systemd-style
credentials directory.

## What changed

- **A path ending in an extension reaches the route that declares it
  (#1431).** Beta.6 added `.md` to the response extensions it removes before
  matching, so `/projects/7/insights/overview.md` was matched as
  `/projects/7/insights/overview` and could land on a later `get "/*"`
  catch-all. A route that spells the extension in its own path, such as
  `get "/projects/:project_id/insights/overview.md"` or
  `get "/guides/setup(.md)"`, now answers first. A path that no route
  declares still has its extension removed, so `/users/1.json` matches
  `/users/:id`. A route's request constraint is asked once per request,
  and a constraint that reads `request.params` sees that route's
  parameters.
- **The request body stays readable after Amber parses a form (#1429).** A
  controller behind the CSRF pipe can read `request.body` again; the bytes
  are handed back from the bounded parse. A multipart body is restored up
  to `params.max_multipart_restore_bytes` (8 MiB by default, `0` turns it
  off) when its `Content-Length` is declared and within that limit and
  `params.max_multipart_body_bytes`; any other multipart body stays drained.
- **Upload tempfiles are deleted when the request finishes (#1429).** To
  keep an upload, call `Amber::Router::File#move_to(path)` during the
  action, or `#retain!` to keep the tempfile at `#path` and delete it
  yourself, for example after a background job.
- **Custom config sections load as raw YAML (#1430).** Amber no longer
  deserializes a custom section through every `YAML::Serializable` type, so
  an application whose Grant models have UUID columns compiles with custom
  config again. `AppConfig#custom` reads a section as the requested type or
  returns its registered default; an unregistered key raises
  `Amber::Exceptions::ConfigurationError`.
- **Settings load at first use (#1424).** `require "amber"` no longer reads
  settings, so a section registered in `config/initializers` reads its YAML
  value, and `config/application.cr` can still set `Amber.path` and
  `Amber.env`. Amber colors its own log lines from `logging.colorize` and
  leaves the global `Colorize.enabled` flag alone.
- **Request parameters are bounded (#1419).** Counts, nesting depth, key
  and value sizes, body sizes, array indices and padding, multipart parts,
  uploads and WebSocket messages each have a limit in the new `params:`
  section of `config/environments/<env>.yml` (or `AMBER_PARAMS_<KEY>`). An
  HTTP request beyond a limit is answered with `400 Bad Request`; a
  WebSocket message over `max_websocket_message_bytes` (2 MiB) closes the
  connection with code 1009. The defaults and every limit are listed in
  `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Credentials directory (#1423).** `Amber::Configuration.register_credentials`
  reads a systemd-style credentials directory, one file per credential, into
  a typed section. The application passes the directory, usually from
  `CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY`, before settings load:

  ```crystal
  if credentials_directory = ENV["CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY"]?
    Amber::Configuration.register_credentials(:credentials, AppCredentials, credentials_directory)
  else
    Amber::Configuration.register(:credentials, AppCredentials)
  end
  ```

  `AMBER_{SECTION}_{KEY}` overrides now reach registered custom sections.
- **A GREEN build (#1421):** no compiler warnings. The ecosystem agent
  context now names Micrate, Gemma and Mica (#1417).

## Fork fixes now in Amber

| Fix | Fork commit | Upstream |
|---|---|---|
| Restore the request body after form parsing | `8c71a57c` | #1429 |
| Delete upload tempfiles at request teardown | `0fbd8eba` | #1429 |
| Read custom config as raw YAML | `bc0d62c6` | #1430 |
| Answer 404 before checking a route's constraint when no route matches | `valid_route?` guard | already in Amber (`7224cb57`) |

An application can drop its fork pin and depend on this release.

## Upgrade

Change the version:

```yaml
dependencies:
  amber:
    github: amberframework/amber
    version: 2.0.0-beta.7
```

Then check three things:

- **Uploads you keep.** An action that keeps an uploaded file past the
  request calls `#move_to` or `#retain!`; otherwise the tempfile is gone
  when the response is sent.
- **Large requests.** A form, JSON body or upload larger than the defaults
  (8 MiB form and document bodies, 64 MiB files, 128 MiB multipart bodies)
  needs its limit raised in `params:`.
- **Custom config readers.** Code that called
  `Amber::Configuration.load_custom_from_yaml` reads sections with
  `Amber.settings.custom(:name, Type)` instead.

Beta.6 also stopped sending `Keep-Alive` response headers (`deb16f8e`); a
spec that expects them needs updating.

## Release

The tag is `v2.0.0-beta.7`. The GitHub release for the tag states the tagged
commit hash, its tree hash, and the sha256 of the source tarball attached to
the release (`scripts/release_checksums.sh v2.0.0-beta.7` produces all three).
A file cannot carry its own tarball's hash, so they live in the release.

## Minecart 2025.11.25.8

Minecart is a drop-in compatible fork of [Crystal Shards](https://github.com/crystal-lang/shards), formerly distributed as `shards-alpha`.

- Builds on Windows: MCP server process checks use `Process.exists?`, and stopping a server uses `taskkill` on Windows and signals elsewhere.
- Includes 2025.11.25.7: the Minecart name (`shards-alpha` remains as an alias binary), library range declarations in the policy file, commit-pinned molinillo and mcprotocol, and a `git archive` source tarball with a SHA-256 sidecar.

Asset Pipeline 0.37.0 removes a major production gap for Amber V2 applications: static assets beyond CSS and JavaScript now participate in the same deterministic build contract.

### What ships

- Recursively fingerprints images, fonts, CSS, JavaScript, source maps, and other static files.
- Rewrites local CSS `url(...)` and `@import` references plus JavaScript imports, exports, dynamic imports, and source-map references to fingerprinted outputs.
- Records the full digest, Subresource Integrity value, media type, byte size, and precompressed gzip metadata in a deterministic manifest.
- Verifies the generated directory against that manifest before deployment.
- Safely prunes only outputs owned by the previous manifest and publishes the new manifest last.
- Rejects path traversal, escaping symlinks, missing local references, and other inputs that would make a production build incomplete.
- Uses Windows-safe file discovery and includes a dedicated Windows static-asset job alongside the Linux and macOS matrix.

### Upgrade

Set `asset_pipeline` to `~> 0.37.0`, run `shards update asset_pipeline`, then build and verify your assets before compiling the application:

```console
amber assets build --env production
amber assets check --env production
```

The Amber V2 web template and framework integration use this release directly.

### Validation

- 2,071 web examples passed; 66 pending; no failures.
- Crystal latest passed on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Crystal 1.10.1 passed on Linux and macOS.

Full change: #14

## BREAKING CHANGES

SafeHTML v1 changes `Components::Component#render` from a plain `String` contract to `Components::SafeHTML`. Components and callers that treat rendered markup as an unrestricted string must migrate. This is a breaking 0.x minor release.

The release also enforces unsafe HTML sinks at construction and render time: inline `on*` handlers are banned, URL-bearing attributes require `SafeURL` validation, raw style/script and document-valued bodies use typed doors, malformed attribute names are rejected, and direct mutable-attribute bypasses are revalidated before bytes are emitted.

Migration references:

- [Output contract](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#2-the-contract)
- [Bans and typed safety doors](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#3-the-bans)
- [`raw()` policy](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#4-the-raw-policy)
- [Component migration guide](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#5-migration-guide-for-components)
- [Explicit v1 exclusions](https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/blob/v0.36.0/docs/SAFE_HTML_V1.md#6-whats-out-of-scope-for-v1-and-why)

## Included

- `SafeHTML` output type and `SafeBuffer` construction path.
- `SafeURL`, `SafeStyle`, `SafeSrcSet`, and typed APIs for compound/document sinks.
- A single render-time attribute-validation authority covering alternate mutation paths.
- Adversarial and falsifiability specs for URL, attribute-name, script, style, iframe `srcdoc`, SVG foreign-content, object `data`, and `formaction` cases.
- DataTable migration exemplar and the complete SafeHTML v1 contract/migration document.
- Shard version `0.36.0`, with the complete 12-commit SafeHTML history preserved by merge.

Full changes: https://github.com/amberframework/asset_pipeline/compare/v0.35.0...v0.36.0
